name: Tapp Tarock
description: Tapp Tarock (German: Tapp-Tarock), also called Viennese Tappen or Tappen, is a three-player Austrian tarot trick-taking game using the 54-card Industrie und Glück deck. Each player receives 16 cards and 6 form the talon. Players bid (Dreier, Unterer, Oberer, Solo); the declarer may exchange with three talon cards in lower contracts or play alone in Solo. Play is anticlockwise; follow suit or trump; declarer needs 36 card points to win.
deck: 54-card Industrie und Glück Tarot (22 trumps plus 32 suit cards)

history.origins: Tapp Tarock arose in Austria, possibly in the late 18th century; mentioned in Viennese works by 1806. Oldest rules description dates to 1821.
timeline: Late 18th century: Game likely developed in Austria.
1806: Tarocktappen mentioned in Viennese comic opera and letters.
19th–20th century: Played in Germany and Austria; four-player variants such as Königrufen developed.
history.cultural: Was the preferred card game of Viennese coffee houses before the Anschluss; still played sporadically. Considered a good introduction to Tarock before Cego, Illustrated Tarock, or Königrufen.
history.evolution: Originally had Tapper, Dreier, Solo bids; Tapper (use all six talon cards) was soon dropped. Modern bidding has Dreier, Unterer, Oberer, Solo with optional announcements (win last trick with Trump I, or Valat).

setup.players: Three players. Seating and first dealer may be determined by lot.
setup.deck: 54-card Industrie und Glück Tarot pack: 22 trumps (Sküs, XXI down to I) and 32 suit cards in four French suits (K, Q, Cavalier, Jack, and four pip cards per suit). Black suits rank K>Q>C>J>10>9>8>7; red suits K>Q>C>J>1>2>3>4.
setup.dealing: Dealer shuffles and offers cut. Top six cards are placed face down in two crosswise packets of three as the talon. Then 16 cards to each player anticlockwise in packets of four, starting with forehand (to dealer's right). If the cutter knocks, all 16 are dealt in one packet.
setup.equipment: 54-card Austrian Tarock deck, score sheet or chips.

rules.objective: As declarer, score at least 36 card points (35⅔ rounded up) from tricks and talon to win the contract; defenders win if declarer fails. Optional announcements (win last trick with Trump I, or Valat) add bonus risk and reward.
rules.gameplay: Bidding: Forehand opens; players pass or bid Dreier, Unterer, Oberer, or Solo in ascending order; overcall or hold. Highest bidder is declarer. In Dreier/Unterer/Oberer the declarer exposes both talon halves, picks one, discards three cards (no Kings or Trull; tarocks only if no option, then shown to defenders); unused half counts to defenders. In Solo, talon is set aside for defenders. Announcements: win last trick with Trump I, or Valat (win every trick). Play: Anticlockwise from forehand. Must follow suit if able; otherwise must play a trump; otherwise may discard. Scoring: Tarock packet scheme; declarer needs 36+ points to win.
keyRules: Follow suit if able; otherwise trump; otherwise discard.
Declarer needs 36 card points to win (70 total, 35⅔ rounded up).
Discards may not include Kings or Trull (Sküs, Mond, or Trump I).
Game values: Dreier 3, Unterer 4, Oberer 5, Solo 8, Valat 12 or 24 if announced.

strategy.basic: As declarer, use the talon to strengthen trumps and void a suit for ruffing. As defenders, coordinate to force declarer to use high trumps early.
strategy.intermediate: Track trumps and honours (Sküs, Mond, and Trump I) to time winning the last trick with Trump I or to prevent it. In Solo, declarer must plan without talon help.
strategy.advanced: Bidding and hold strategy: bid only when hand and talon potential justify the contract; defenders should communicate through leads.
tips: Pagat Ultimo is high risk and reward; announce only with strong control.
In Dreier/Unterer/Oberer, choose the talon half that best improves your hand.

scoring.description: Card points in packets of three, 2 deducted per packet; declarer needs 36 (35⅔ rounded up) to win. Game values: Dreier 3, Unterer 4, Oberer 5, Solo 8, Valat 12 or 24 announced. Bonuses for Köpfe, Tarock Trull, Royal Trull, Pagat Ultimo, Valat.
scoring.winCondition: Declarer wins by taking 36+ card points; defenders win if declarer fails. Optional announcements add bonus points.
